t: Why I write about science, capital and execution
s: A working notebook for translating between the languages that keep research apart from companies, deals and investment.
b: For the last few years I have worked where research, intellectual property, market, finance and execution meet. At that junction I have seen the same pattern again and again: the science is good, but it never becomes a company, a licence or an investment, because every party speaks a different language. This blog is my working notebook for translating between those languages. # What you will find here Technology transfer: how a deal is structured, what each side negotiates and where it usually breaks. Science spin-offs: governance, valuation and capital readiness. Technology valuation: ranges, assumptions and negotiation anchors. Ecosystems: universities, companies, investors and public institutions moving in the same direction. # How I write I write from real cases, without disclosing confidential information. Every article will try to leave you something usable: a framework, a checklist or a question for your next board meeting. Key point Complexity becomes valuable only when it can be translated into a decision, a deal and a path to scale. If you want to suggest a topic or discuss a case, write to me at vmrlbiz@gmail.com or on LinkedIn .
